verdict: Entergy rode a hot summer and fast-growing industrial demand to a 15% revenue jump and $940M of profit, and raised the floor of its full-year outlook.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP, diluted)
kpis.note: Same as adjusted EPS; vs $1.53 a year ago

segments.name: Residential
segments.note: Homes across Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas — a hot summer meant more air conditioning and higher bills.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.note: Shops, offices and other businesses buying electricity.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.note: Factories, refineries and fast-ramping data centers and primary-metals customers — industrial sales volumes rose 4.9% in the quarter.

segments.name: Other electric revenues
segments.note: Regulatory and other electric revenues outside the main customer classes, including rate-related credits and adjustments.

segments.name: Sales for resale
segments.note: Wholesale electricity sold to other utilities and power markets.

segments.name: Governmental & other
segments.note: Government customers ($81M) plus other utility and miscellaneous revenues ($23M).

opex.name: Other operation & maintenance
opex.note: Running plants and wires day to day ($833M), plus $30M of nuclear refueling outage costs.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of power plants and grid assets over their long lives.

opex.name: Taxes other than income taxes
opex.note: Property and similar taxes across four states.

opex.name: Decommissioning & regulatory, net
opex.note: $60M for retiring nuclear plants, partly offset by $21M of net regulatory credits.

otherDetail: Other income of $179M — a $61M allowance for equity funds used during construction (AFUDC, a regulated credit for money tied up in building), $100M of interest and investment income and $17M miscellaneous — less $436M of net interest expense, for net other expense of $257M.

takeaways.title: Profit jumped on heat and growth
takeaways.text: GAAP and adjusted EPS were both $1.98, up from $1.53 a year ago. The utility business earned $1,079M, helped by favorable weather, higher retail volumes and regulatory rate actions.

takeaways.title: Big customers are ramping
takeaways.text: Industrial sales volumes rose 4.9% in the quarter and 9.6% year to date as data-center and primary-metals customers ramp up. Entergy also expanded its service agreement with Google in Arkansas.

takeaways.title: Dividend up, building plan up
takeaways.text: The quarterly dividend rose 6% to $0.68 a share, and the 2026–2030 capital plan grew by $1.5B — more grid and generation to serve the new load.

oneTimers: There were no special items in Q3 2026: GAAP earnings of $940M (attributable) exactly matched adjusted earnings. Year to date, adjusted earnings add back a $14M item, so nine-month adjusted profit is $1,821M vs $1,808M GAAP.
footerNote: Utility layout: fuel, fuel-related expenses and gas purchased for resale ($726M) plus purchased power ($464M) are treated as the cost of revenue; the remaining operating lines mirror Entergy's income statement. Net income in the flow is the consolidated $945M; $940M was attributable to Entergy Corporation after $5M of preferred dividends and noncontrolling interests, matching the $1.98 diluted EPS. Segment revenues are Entergy's customer-class electric revenues from its Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.
